content.text: Capturing some conversation from slack channel that might be helpful in approaching this ticket:
acoburn [2:11 PM]
the namespace issue is actually really, really easy if you just stop using JCR namespaces
if the persistence layer uses full IRIs, then you just add in prefixes (if at all) in a post-processing step
you can have the prefixes defined in a simple file if you want
whikloj [2:12 PM]
Yeah, the question we had was whether we add the prefixes or not and if you do how does one alter that mapping
acoburn [2:12 PM]
as for
how
, it's just a method you call on the Jena writer
you pass it a Map<String, String>
as for how to create that `Map<String, String>`, there are a million ways to do that
in Trellis, I just read a JSON file
I also have a namespace impl that uses ZooKeeper for full horizontal distribution, and even that wasn't too complex
birkland [2:15 PM]
A simple JSON mapping file would work well,
and
not risk :boom: your repository by messing with a dangerous CND file.
acoburn [2:15 PM]
I've only seen bad things happen when you allow an admin to modify an CND file
https://github.com/trellis-ldp/trellis/blob/master/components/io-jena/src/main/java/org/trellisldp/io/JenaIOService.java#L160-L164
https://github.com/trellis-ldp/trellis/blob/master/components/io-jena/src/main/java/org/trellisldp/io/JenaIOService.java#L167-L169
My understanding currently is:
to store info about a node in modeshape, you have to store it in jcr properties.
properties are identified with prefixed paths (i.e., fedora:lastModifiedBy).
The prefix must be in modeshapes baked-in namespace registry
We want to store full URIs for properties and control the prefixes outside of modeshape
modeshape won't accept a property named "
http://example.com/property
" because "http" is not a known prefix.
So unless there is a way to store info in modeshape that I’m not seeing in its API, it seems like three options are:
Prefix predicate URIs prior to persistence, then have jena handle namespacing from a configuration file. For example, modeshape stores a predicate named “pred:http:%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fproperty”
Leave modeshape’s namespace registry alone. Change the serialization of triples to translate out of modeshape prefixes into full urls, then switch to prefixes from the provided configuration.
Leave modeshape’s namespace registry alone. When serializing triples return full URIs.
I don't think any of these approaches has any impact on POST/PATCH/PUT requests, since the prefixes there are handled internally by jena and received by fedora as URIs.
:  in the case of 1,  how do you envision the behavior in the case that a namespace prefix is not configured?
: in  case 1,  that would involve storing more information no,  since the whole URI would be stored in Modeshape?
If a namespace prefix isn't configured you would get back the full uri rather than a prefixed predicate. That should be the case for #1 or #2
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1425
Resolved by
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/cd3341a9bcd7d19055fe40319bc3237bc1eff54a
This ticket is to determine the best path forward to deprecating the use of the Modeshape Namespace registry.
This could mean returning full URIs in all responses or replacing it with some other option.
Once a path is determined then this ticket can move to implement it.

  2. Leave modeshape’s namespace registry alone. Change the serialization of triples to translate out of modeshape prefixes into full urls, then switch to prefixes from the provided configuration.
